claims.text: The investigated alloy has composition Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Very rapid cooling can produce an amorphous Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 structure.
The rapidly cooled amorphous alloy has poor thermal stability under standard reheating because of extensive primary crystallization.
Ultra-fast reheating followed by a short sub-onset isothermal hold will increase amorphous retention.
Ultra-fast reheating followed by a short sub-onset isothermal hold will improve thermal stability.
Approximately 960-1341 K defines a suitable reheating interval just below primary crystallization onset.
The reheating treatment causes atomic-scale structural relaxation within the amorphous phase.
The reheating treatment kinetically suppresses primary nucleation.
The short isothermal hold lowers the free energy of the amorphous phase through structural relaxation.
A hold just below the proposed onset does not supply enough thermal energy to overcome the crystallization activation barrier.
Suppressing primary nucleation delays formation of the primary crystalline phases.
Relative to conventional reheating, the tailored protocol will retain a higher amorphous phase fraction.
Relative to conventional reheating, the tailored protocol will shift crystallization onset to a higher temperature or otherwise delay crystallization.
The intervention remains effective provided the treatment does not exceed approximately 1341 K.
Processing immediately after rapid cooling prevents spontaneous nucleation.
XRD and TEM can distinguish the amorphous structure from crystalline products in this alloy.

contradictions.description: The treatment is described as operating between 960 and 1341 K while remaining strictly below crystallization onset, but the cited values are distinct cooling/solidification transformation temperatures rather than a demonstrated reheating onset. If onset were near the lower end of that interval, much of the proposed interval would not be below onset.
